# PNG to ICO

- Route: `/tools/png-to-ico`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `image`
- Slug: `png-to-ico`

## Summary

Turn a PNG into a real multi-size .ico favicon for websites and Windows app icons. (Image tools)

## Details

A favicon needs to be a real .ico file containing several sizes so browsers and Windows can pick the right one. Media Manipulator generates a genuine multi-size ICO from your PNG — not a renamed file — packing the standard 16–256 px icon ladder.
### What it does
- Generates a real .ico container from a PNG image.
- Packs multiple sizes (16, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256 px) into one file.
- Preserves transparency so the icon sits cleanly on any background.
- Produces a file browsers and Windows accept as a favicon/app icon.
### How to use it
1. Upload PNG: Drop in a PNG — a square image gives the best icon.
2. Generate sizes: We render each standard icon size from your image.
3. Pack ICO: The sizes are packed into one real .ico container.
4. Download ICO: Save favicon.ico for your site or app.
### Supported formats
- Input: png, jpg, webp
- Output: ico
- A multi-size ICO (16/32/48/64/128/256 px) is generated. Start from a square image for the best result.
### Technical details
- The ICO is built with ImageMagick’s icon auto-resize, producing a true multi-image container — not a renamed PNG.
- Including several sizes lets browsers and Windows pick the sharpest icon for each context (tab, taskbar, desktop).
- For the cleanest result, start from a square PNG at 256×256 or larger so every size downsamples crisply.
### Use cases
- Website favicons: Generate favicon.ico for your site’s tab icon.
- Windows app icons: Create an .ico for a desktop application.
- Shortcuts: Make a crisp icon for a desktop shortcut.
- Branding: Turn a logo PNG into a proper icon file.
### FAQ
Q: How do I convert a PNG to ICO for free?
A: Upload your .png above and click convert — you get a real multi-size .ico back.
Q: Is this a real ICO or a renamed PNG?
A: A real ICO. We generate several icon sizes and pack them into a true .ico container, which is what browsers and Windows expect.
Q: What sizes are included?
A: The standard favicon ladder: 16, 32, 48, 64, 128, and 256 px. Browsers and Windows pick the best size for each context.
Q: What image works best?
A: A square PNG at 256×256 or larger gives the crispest result, since every smaller size downsamples cleanly from it.
